title: observability: token-level cost/latency dashboards + tracing/logging enhancements
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Add token-level cost and latency breakdown dashboards, enhance tracing spans for inference requests, improve logging request enrichment, and tune related alerts to reduce noise. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context: Customers and platform teams need finer-grained visibility into token-level unit economics (cost/token) and latency contribution during inference, plus better tracing and logs to correlate regressions. This PR adds token-level cost/latency metrics, Grafana dashboards, tracing span improvements, logging enrichment, and a first-pass alert tuning to reduce noisy SRE pages.

What this changes: - Metrics: emit per-request token counts, per-token compute cost estimate (cpu/gpu/kv components), prefix vs generation latency breakdown, cache hit/miss counters (kv cache), and model-variant tags where applicable. Metric names are prefixed with redwood.inference.* and follow our metrics naming conventions. Implemented cardinality controls and tag sanitization to avoid high-cardinality explosion.
- Dashboards: new Grafana dashboards (token-cost-latency, kv-cache-overview) with p50/p95/p99 token latency heatmaps, cost per 1k tokens, and per-route cost breakdowns. Embedded links to trace samples.
- Tracing: expand span instrumentation for key phases (request.decode -> prefix.lookup -> model.forward -> decode.postprocess). Add model_variant, route_id, and quantization_profile as span attributes to help root-cause.
- Logging: enrich request logs with request_id, model_variant, route_id, and token_count; improve structured logging schema to be compatible with existing log parsers.
- Alerts: tuned cost/latency alerts to use group_by by route and model_variant with new thresholds; added suppression window for known bursty routes; updated runbook links.

Testing and validation: unit tests for metric emission and tag sanitization added; e2e run on staging evaluated dashboards against synthetic workloads; traces verified in Jaeger/Tempo and sample logs parsed in staging ELK. Initial CI run surfaced a flaky integration test (tests/e2e/test_kv_cache.py) which was fixed by adding a deterministic seed and retry; final CI run passed.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind observability.feature_token_metrics flag; dashboards deployed to staging and then promoted to prod during a low-traffic window. Configurable alert thresholds default to conservative values; SRE will monitor for one week before tightening.

Migration notes: existing dashboards referencing earlier token metrics will continue to work; new dashboards are additive. Cost estimates are approximate and documented in docs/observability/token_metrics.md.

Related: ENG-4829 (token-level metrics design), ENG-4890 (kv cache metric schema), SUP-2311 (support request requesting per-route cost breakout).

Samira Patel: Made suppression window configurable in observability-config.yaml and added per-route overrides; defaults remain conservative.
Daniel Kim: Could we include example queries for Datadog/Grafana in the docs so on-call can quickly validate?
Samira Patel: Added example queries and dashboard links to docs/observability/token_metrics.md (section 'Troubleshooting & quick checks').
Priya Rao: unit tests + e2e on staging look good — approving.
Liam O'Connor: Verified trace attributes and sample traces in staging; small nit about naming consistency fixed. Approving.

notes_for_ops: Feature gated: enable observability.feature_token_metrics in prod via config map to start ingestion.
Monitor new metric redwood.inference.token_latency.p95 and redwood.inference.cost_per_1k_tokens for first 72h.
If alert noise increases, adjust monitoring/alerts/token_cost_alerts.yaml suppression windows per-route.
Backfill: cost estimates are not backfilled automatically; to backfill, run scripts/metrics/backfill_token_costs.py against historical request logs.
